description.value: The study examined the prevalence and clinical associations of posterior cingulate cortex hypometabolism in Alzheimer's disease, behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia, and cognitively normal subjects using [18F]FDG-PET.

posterior cingulate cortex (PCC)
the PCC (defined using anatomical boundaries that are described elsewhere ( Minoshima et al., 1994 ))

PCC hypometabolism was considered to be present when the PCC (defined using anatomical boundaries that are described elsewhere ( Minoshima et al., 1994 )) was isointense – since healthy brain metabolism is associated with highest glucose uptake in the PCC ( Loessner et al., 1995 ) – or hypointense compared with other cortical regions by thresholding the SUVr image to identify the area in the brain with the highest activity concentration ( Minoshima et al., 1997 ).

description.value: CSF tau/Aβ and CSF Aβ measurements used to assess likelihood of underlying Alzheimer's disease or amyloid pathology and to define diagnostic groups.
Standard neuropsychological test battery assessing major cognitive functions, including compound scores for cognitive domains, MMSE, CDR, and NPI.
MRI assessment used to identify abnormalities indicative of neurodegeneration and for co-registration, segmentation, and region-of-interest definition.
Visual reading by two nuclear medicine physicians to assess the presence of posterior cingulate cortex hypometabolism.
